newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela widens Coca-Cola monopoly case.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela widens Coca-Cola monopoly case.

text.p: Venezuela's anti-trust body Procompetencia said on Friday that it had widened its investigation into PepsiCo charge that Coca-Cola now holds a monopoly in the market.

Procompetencia said in a release that it had opened new proceedings against Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Co and the newly- created joint venture Coca-Cola-Hit de Venezuela, which overturned Pepsi's dominance of the Venezuelan market.

Previously, Procompetencia's investigations into the soft drinks war had only cited local bottler Hit de Venezuela, owned by the Cisneros Group, which switched allegiance from Pepsi to Coca-Cola in mid-August.
Pepsi has argued that the Cisneros Group's decision to drop a 47-year-old franchise agreement for a joint venture with Coca Cola created a monopoly.

Pepsi, which was left without any bottling facilities in the country, has virtually disappeared from grocery stores and supermarkets. Procompetencia said it would reach a final decision over the soft-drink monopoly by mid-December.

Procompetencia added that it had overturned a previous decision to prevent Coca-Cola from selling off cases of Pepsi held in bottling plants worth 2.053 billion ($4.3 million) since the product was beginning to deteriorate.
Pepsi officials have said the company will invest $400 million in Venezuela over the next four years in an effort to reclaim the market it dominated until last month.
Local media reports have said Pepsi has arranged a deal with local brewer Polar to use its bottling facilities, but Pepsi officials have not confirmed the deal.
